sermon.title: Moral Mutiny
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer defines America’s moral mutiny since the 1960s and walks through Ahaz in Chronicles and Isaiah as a pattern of leaders who encourage decline—child sacrifice, mixing religions, bad laws and silence. He cites crime, abortion, STD and illiteracy statistics as spoken, calls for a mutiny for morality, and warns God will bring a nation low if the honest stay silent.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Many statistics (621k molested, 1.3M abortions, 50% STD, illiteracy %, etc.) given without sources—flag all unverified. Same-sex marriage/SCOTUS, homosexuality in schools, prosperity gospel, personal court fight kept as spoken. Series paired with Moral Advancement.

faqs.question: When does he say America’s moral mutiny began?
faqs.answer: Since the 1960s, a rebellion against morality.

faqs.question: Which verse says Ahaz encouraged moral decline?
faqs.answer: Second Chronicles 28:19—the Lord brought Judah low because of Ahaz who encouraged moral decline.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For the LORD brought Judah low because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had encouraged moral decline in Judah and had been continually unfaithful to the LORD.

faqs.question: Did Ahaz’s father Jotham do right?
faqs.answer: Second Chronicles 27:2: Jotham did what was right in the sight of the Lord, yet the people still acted corruptly; Ahaz encouraged more.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done (although he did not enter the temple of the LORD). But still the people acted corruptly.

faqs.question: How many abortions does he cite per year?
faqs.answer: 1.3 million babies aborted each year as a contraceptive, on demand—statistic as spoken, unverified.

faqs.question: What STD statistic does he cite?
faqs.answer: He says 50% of Americans have a sexually transmitted disease because sex is treated as unrestricted choice—unverified as spoken.

faqs.question: What illiteracy figures does he cite?
faqs.answer: 19% of high school graduates cannot read; 85% of unwed mothers and 68% of those arrested are illiterate—as spoken, unverified.

faqs.question: Did he personally fight government pressure on a Christian school?
faqs.answer: He says in his early days they tried taxing the church over a Christian school; media painted him as a weirdo; they went to court and won.

faqs.question: What does Isaiah 10:1–2 say about lawmakers?
faqs.answer: Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees that restrain the right and leave the poor unprotected.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, Who write misfortune, Which they have prescribed To rob the needy of justice, And to take what is right from the poor of My people, That widows may be their prey, And that they may rob the fatherless.

faqs.question: Does he say the Supreme Court has authority to legalize same-sex marriage?
faqs.answer: He says it has neither constitutional authority nor common moral standards authority.

faqs.question: Will God judge America for silence?
faqs.answer: He says God will bring a nation low, including America, if honest good moral people stay silent.
